item.title: Bijan Robinson Tells Recruits To Ignore NIL Cash For 40-Year Future
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Bijan Robinson is telling young athletes to stop chasing the biggest check and start looking at the whole picture. The Falcons running back knows exactly what it takes to make it, and he is not happy with the current mindset in college recruiting. He warns that cash is pulling kids away from the coaches who actually care about their future. This is not just advice for high schoolers; it is a warning for the entire league. The Distraction of Quick Cash Robinson played high school football before the name, image, and likeness era took over the sports world. He sees a major problem today where athletes pick schools based on the payout rather than the plan. “I think money has been very much of a distraction for kids,” Robinson said in an interview with Sports Illustrated . He believes players are ignoring the relationships that help them grow. If a recruit spends all their time counting dollars instead of talking to coaches, they are making a huge mistake. The money comes and goes, but the right mentor stays with you forever. He remembers his own path from Tucson to Texas. He did not think he needed to go to a big school to get noticed, but he was wrong. Arizona offered him a scholarship after just five varsity games. More offers came later, and he realized the coaches were coming to him. He did not have to chase the money to get the chance. He just had to be ready when the right people showed up. Thinking Four Decades Ahead The most important lesson Robinson learned came from his former high school coach, Dennis Bene. The two talked about life after football long before Robinson ever stepped on an NFL field. Bene taught him to look past the next three years of college ball. “The decision I was making was not just gonna be for a three-year decision, but gonna be for a 40-year decision,” Robinson recalled. That shift in thinking changed everything for him. It is about building a life that lasts, not just a season that ends in May. Bene was more than a coach to Robinson; he was a father figure who checked on his life off the field too. “Not only was he just a father figure for me, but he was a guy that always just made sure that I was doing great things off the field and on the field,” Robinson said. That kind of support is rare, and it is exactly what kids need to hear now. Chasing a NIL deal might pay for a new car, but a good coach pays for a future. Proof That the Work Pays Off Robinson is living proof that his advice works. He is putting up MVP numbers this season for the Falcons, even with a shaky team start. Yahoo Sports reports that over seven games, he has accumulated 704 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 131 carries. He also has 25 receptions for 203 yards and one more touchdown. His total yards from scrimmage sit at 907, and he is averaging 129.6 yards per game. That is elite production, and it did not come from picking the school with the most cash. item.title: PFF: 5 lowest-graded Jets players on defense in Week 7 vs. Dolphins
item.description: Well, let's just say it wasn't the performance everyone expected. If any game was set up well for the New York Jets to win and gain traction, it would have been the Week 7 matchup. The winless Miami Dolphins were in town. The home crowd at MetLife Stadium was ready to be engaged and make life hard for the visitors. Instead, New York laid an egg. Miami didn't just open the scoring to take their first lead of the season. They never trailed, and they left town with a 28-25 win , one that doubles as their first triumph of the season. The final score doesn't reflect how lopsided this one felt. Aaron Glenn is under fire . So is his team. Pro Football Focus' player grades offer another perspective on Sunday's performance . Here's a look at the lowest-graded players on the defensive side of the ball before everyone turns the page and looks ahead to Week 8 and the Las Vegas Raiders . The Jets are looking to improve their record to 3-5 in that one. Jets' lowest-graded defensive stars in Week 7 5. Harrison Phillips, defensive tackle - 55.4 4. Jowon Briggs, defensive tackle - 45.3 3. Andre Cisco, safety - 44.8 2. Dane Belton, safety - 40.1 1. David Bailey, EDGE - 39.3 This article originally appeared on Jets Wire: PFF: 5 lowest-graded Jets players on defense in Week 7 vs. Dolphins

item.title: Josh Simmons reportedly asked to leave meeting by Patrick Mahomes, Andy Reid
item.description: Former Ohio State offensive lineman Josh Simmons was asked to leave a Kansas City Chiefs team meeting by quarterback Patrick Mahomes and head coach Andy Reid, according to NFL Network insiders Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo . "There are a lot of questions about Josh Simmons, who is as talented as a left tackle as you can possibly get," Rappaport said. "He is a stud as a player. I don't know if he plays for the Chiefs again. I don't know when he plays for the Chiefs again." Those comments aired on ESPN's "Big Day with Peter Schrager," Oct. 27. Per the initial report , published on Oct. 25, Simmons was sitting with his feet up in the offense's meeting room when Reid asked Simmons to put his feet down. Simmons pushed back, saying he had to sit that way due to back and hip pain, so Reid told Simmons to leave and get treatment, which Mahomes echoed. Simmons apologized to Reid and team leadership later in the day, telling them he could've handled the situation better, according to the report. Simmons has yet to play for the Chiefs this season due to a bulging disc in his back. He returned to practice during the Chiefs' Week 5 off week, but missed practice on Oct. 25, with the Chiefs listing his absence as "back/not injury related-personal." According to the report, the incident in the meeting room occurred that same day. The Chiefs placed Simmons on injured reserve on Oct. 26. The earliest he can return is Week 11 of the NFL season. The Chiefs selected Simmons with the 32nd overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. He played in eight games his rookie year. After missing a chunk of games due to family/personal reasons, Simmons then dislocated and fractured his wrist against the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. He underwent surgery and missed the rest of the season. "I don't know if he plays for the Chiefs again." - @RapSheet on Josh Simmons on @BigDayESPN pic.twitter.com/wLp5Ot2aBb — Peter Schrager (@PSchrags) October 27, 2026 Simmons transferred to the Buckeyes after his sophomore year with San Diego State. Before Ohio State won the national championship during Simmons' senior year, he tore his patellar tendon when the Buckeyes lost to Oregon on Oct. 12, 2024. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Josh Simmons reportedly asked to leave meeting by Patrick Mahomes, Andy Reid

item.title: Smotherman Wins Bermuda Playoff To Cement Autumn Dominance
item.description: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images Austin Smotherman has officially turned the fall season into his personal playground. Having gone 99 times without a PGA Tour win, the 32-year-old has now secured two victories within 101 career starts. This rapid turnaround began at the Bank of Utah Championship and concluded on Monday morning in Bermuda. The win at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship was not just a career milestone; it was a statement made under pressure and high winds at Port Royal Golf Course. The path to the trophy was complicated by weather. High winds forced the cancellation of Sunday’s final round, reducing the tournament to 54 holes. According to the Fulton Sun, Smotherman and Seamus Power finished regulation play level on 16-under par, requiring a sudden-death playoff to decide the champion. Monday morning saw the two competitors return, where they both recorded pars on their initial two trips to the par-three 16th hole. The drama ended on the third extra hole when Smotherman secured the title with another par. Because Power missed the green, he could not salvage par from the rough; his chip reached 16 feet, yet the putt was missed. A Titleist Sweep and Statistical Dominance The victory highlights a massive surge for Titleist equipment this season. Golf Retailing reports that Smotherman defeated Power in an all-Titleist Pro V1x playoff, marking the 29th PGA Tour victory of the year for a player using their golf balls. Smotherman carded rounds of 65, 66, and 66 during the event, recording 17 birdies and an eagle. Power reached the same total score with rounds of 66, 64, and 67. The leaderboard clearly showed dominance, with Titleist ball players filling the first nine spots. Sixteen players utilized the next-generation balls in Bermuda while the brand extended its validation programme across the professional tours. Smotherman’s mental approach remained steady despite the chaotic schedule. He noted in an interview with the Fulton Sun, “We’re out here playing an incredible sport in a beautiful spot. Whatever things are going to be thrown at us, (caddie Zak Williamson) and I were going to be on top of our game.” He added that the communication from the tour regarding the weather delay helped them prepare. “Once we got that news it was nice to know what’s going on. To come out on top is a cherry on top of that, so pretty awesome,” Smotherman said. The Playoff Breakdown and Next Steps Seamus Power, seeking his third career PGA Tour title, fell short in the playoff. He admitted the conditions played a role in his loss. “Hit some good shots in the playoff, just didn’t quite judge the wind right, but that’s golf sometimes. I’ll move onwards,” Power said. His sentiment reflected the difficulty of the day, noting, “Had a chance this morning, wasn’t able to do it, which is disappointing, but overall great week, can’t complain too much.” While Power navigated the wind poorly on the final hole, Smotherman capitalized on the opportunity to close out the even

item.title: UConn men's basketball hosts Purdue in final preseason exhibition: Live updates, analysis
item.description: EAST LANSING, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Silas Demary Jr. #5 of the UConn Huskies dribbles the ball past Jordan Scott #6 of the Michigan State Spartans in the second half at Breslin Center on October 20, 2026 in East Lansing, Michigan. (Photo by Rey Del Rio/Getty Images) (Rey Del Rio/Getty Images) UConn men's basketball will round out its three-game exhibition schedule Tuesday evening with another stiff test against Purdue at PeoplesBank Arena in Hartford. The Huskies stand undefeated in preseason action, cruising past Gerry McNamara's new-look Syracuse side 72-52 before heading to East Lansing to secure an eight-point win over Michigan State. Meanwhile, Dan Hurley's sqaud will provide Purdue's first major test this season, as the Boilermakers arrive in Hartford after playing Ball State and Purdue-Fort Wayne. Here's everything you need to know about Tuesday's action: How to watch UConn vs Purdue The Huskies and Boilermakers will face off at 7:03 p.m. ET from PeoplesBank Arena. The game will be broadcast locally on WFSB, a CBS affiliate that airs in all Connecticut counties except for Fairfield. Fans can also stream the action on UConn+ for a one-time pay-per-view fee of $9.99 or listen via radio on the UConn Sports Network. UConn-Purdue officials announced UConn's exhibitions give both the Huskies roster and Hurley a chance to ramp up into regular-season form, with the two-time national champion looking his usual animated self on the sideline against Syracuse and Michigan State. Hurley will bark at a few familiar faces tonight, with John Gaffney, Tim Clougherty and Matt Potter set to officiate Tuesday's game. Purdue matchup preview It's a new era for coach Matt Painter in West Lafayette this season after losing a pair of multi-year stars: two-time consensus All-American Braden Smith graduated and joined the Indiana Pacers, while double-double machine Trey Kauffman-Renn was granted a temporary restraining order to play a fifth season after signing with Kansas. Caden Pierce, a former Princeton star who UConn fans may remember as a one-time transfer target, averaged 11 points, seven rebounds and three assists in his final season with the Tigers and is the only Boilermaker with a double-digit scoring record. He'll play alongside a promising young backcourt of C.J. Cox, Omer Mayer and Gicarri Harris, looking to feed the next incarnation in a long line of towering Purdue post players: 7-foot-4 Daniel Jacobsen. Injury update: Braylon Mullins will return Star sophomore Braylon Mullins has not participated in either of UConn's exhibitions due to an undisclosed, lingering off-season injury, but Dan Hurley stated in his media availability Monday that the Indiana native will make his debut against Purdue. Hurley added that the entire team is healthy outside of Solo Ball. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. Get the biggest headlines of the day from our network of journalists around the state. This article originally published at UConn men's bask

item.title: Brewers manager Pat Murphy recalls heart attack scare, ponders a new tattoo
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL — Pat Murphy has been thinking about getting a new tattoo and he's been looking for inspiration on what kind to get. He may have found it. In his pregame press conference Tuesday afternoon, Oct. 27, before Game 4 of the World Series, the Milwaukee Brewers manager was asked about surviving a heart attack six years ago. More: Brewers bench coach Pat Murphy on surviving a heart attack and getting a second chance And Murph being Murph, launched into a story. "I swore I wasn't having a heart attack. The ambulance driver, wherever he is, the ambulance driver out there that was in the back of the ambulance that day, I apologize," Murphy began. "It's the first time I've apologized on the record because this ambulance driver was like, ' sir, can I have your next of kin?' "I'm like, bro, next of kin? I'm not going anywhere. You don't need to know my next of kin. OK? 'Would you like to donate your organs?' "I'm like are you (expletive) me? Did you just ask me that? "I showed him pictures of my kids. 'I don't know about you, but I ain't going anywhere. Just chill down on that thing.'" Murphy suffered the heart attack Aug. 2, 2020, during a Brewers workout, when he was the bench coach. Murphy continued the story from his point of view on the incident with the paramedic. "He was like dead serious. He was like super ripping my shirt off. They're sticking stuff on me. I was making them laugh," said Murphy. "Our trainer was there, Scott Barringer at the time, and he was white as a ghost. He didn't know what to think. I'm just joking with the guy like what are we doing here? "Then I got in the room, and all these people are lined up with these white coats on and gloves. And I said, you people are way too serious right now. Whatever you got going on, let's chill out a little bit. This is going to be fine. I'm doing good. "That's the last I remember. I think they shot something in my IV, and that was it." It was a philosophical moment for the 67-year-old coach. "Yeah, I don't know if it changed me at all. It always does when you think about the seriousness of when you're raising kids, you know what I mean? I got two young ones so I can't go anywhere yet," said Murphy. "When those two young ones are at a little better stage, I can shut the curtain. "The perspective is always there. Remember, 'man you were dust and to dust you shall return.' All us Catholics we've heard that. I actually might get that as a tattoo. What do you think? "I was thinking about getting a tattoo for the season, and that could be a good one. 2026, remember, man, you're dust and to dust you shall return." This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Brewers manager Pat Murphy recalls heart attack scare, ponders a new tattoo

item.title: Canelo vs Mbilli: Start time, undercard and how to watch fight this weekend
item.description: Canelo Alvarez will return to the ring this weekend, challenging Christian Mbilli for the WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh . Although the Saudi city has been the target of deadly attacks in recent weeks , Canelo has arrived ahead of his first fight in 13 months , after he was outpointed by fellow great Terence Crawford in Las Vegas. Against Mbilli, the 36-year-old Canelo faces a stern task; the Cameroonian is the younger man, at 31, and he enters his first title defence with an unbeaten record. Canelo Alvarez (right) at the weigh-in for his fight with Terence Crawford (Getty) Last time out, on the Canelo vs Crawford undercard, Mbilli fought Lester Martinez to a brutal draw to retain the interim WBC title, but he was later upgraded to regular champion when Crawford retired. Can Canelo prove that he is still among the best in the world? Or, as he returns from elbow surgery, will he show himself to be in the twilight of his great career? Here’s all you need to know. When is the fight? Canelo vs Mbilli will take place on Saturday 31 October at the ANB Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The main card is expected to begin at 6pm GMT (11am PT / 1pm CT / 2pm ET), with main-event ring walks following at 8.30pm GMT (1.30pm PT / 3.30pm CT / 4.30pm ET). How can I watch it? The event will stream live exclusively on DAZN pay-per-view at a cost of £24.99 ($79.99 in the US), and on DAZN Ultimate Tier – which is priced at £24.99 per month. You can purchase the fight or an Ultimate Tier subscription here. Will the event go ahead, and why is this a question? The organisation of the fight card has been the subject of intense speculation in recent weeks, due to numerous deadly attacks on Riyadh’s airports. Per Saudi authorities, more than 300 people have been left injured and at least 21 dead, due to strikes by the Yemen-aligned Houthis. The international airport has reopened, but the US Department of State has urged citizens to “reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia due to risk of drone and missile targeting", while areas near the Yemen border have been listed as such: “do not travel due to terrorism”. A large plume of black smoke rises from the fuel storage area at King Khalid International Airport (Reuters) Despite these attacks, Saudi adviser and boxing matchmaker Turki Alalshikh has continued to promote the fight, and he tweeted earlier this month , “[Canelo] fears nothing,” adding: “My country is home to the two Holy Mosques, land of peace, safety, rich civilisation, deep history and kind-hearted people.” Canelo arrived in Riyadh on Monday and said in a video on Alalshikh’s X account: “I love to be here in Riyadh, and I’m excited to fight on Saturday.” However, one undercard bout might have been cancelled, per journalist Dan Rafael , who said Lindolfo Delgado would “probably not” face Arthur Biyarslanov; Delgado and his team had reportedly not made travel plans, although Biyarslanov had already arrived in Riyadh. item.title: Posada Says Yankees Don’t Want Him Back And He Is Right
item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Jorge Posada does not feel welcome back at the Yankees. He told The New York Post on Tuesday that he believes the organization does not want him there. The five-time World Series champion played his entire 17-year career in The Bronx. Despite his legacy, he says he will not return to help the team because he feels shut out. Posada spoke to reporters Joel Sherman and Jon Heyman on “The Show” podcast. He said he could help, but he doubts the team wants him. “It’s gotta be the right — I mean, I could, but I don’t think they want me there to tell you the truth,” Posada said. This is a sharp break for a man who won five titles with the club. The 2011 Fallout Still Hurts The reason for this distance goes back to his final season. Posada played his last year in 2011. That season was rough for both him and the front office. He was moved from catcher to a part-time designated hitter. He feuded with management over his playing time. “My last season of my career was a really tough one when it comes to handling everything on my part and also the Yankees toward Jorge Posada,” he said. He noted that he never got a chance to fight for his job. According to him, the front office issued the directive rather than then-manager Joe Girardi. While conversing with Girardi, he clarified that he reached out to neither owner Hal Steinbrenner nor general manager Brian Cashman. He said, “I don’t know what happened. I’d rather just move forward.” That pain from 2011 still stops him from walking into spring training today. He described the feeling of going to the stadium now. “I don’t feel welcome when I go there, you know?” Even during spring training, I do not feel like — I am simply like, I do not know, I do not feel welcome. Since I believe they do not want me there, I choose not to go. A legend who gave everything to the team now feels like an outsider in his own home. He Wants Accountability But Not the Job Posada still cares about the team. He thinks the Yankees need a strong voice to push players. He wants higher standards of accountability. He said mental mistakes get magnified during the playoffs. “You didn’t run to first base?” Get him out of the game. Make him understand that this means something. This is really a job, not a game, and certain guys are failing to do their job. He wants someone to say that certain plays are unacceptable. However, he does not blame the current leadership. He said general manager Brian Cashman and manager Aaron Boone are the right people to lead. He stressed that the players are responsible for their own shortcomings. “It’s not on Boonie, it’s not on Cash,” Posada said. Is it on the players? Indeed, because those individuals are the ones who go out there and play the game. He suggested the team could make changes to the coaching staff. They could bring in someone who would push the players. But that person will not be him. He is too old to go back and feel that rejection again. “So it’s tough to go back and

item.title: Arsenal stunned by fourth-tier Fleetwood as underdogs win shoot-out
item.description: Fleetwood Town's Aaron Loupalo-Bi (2nd L) celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the English Carabao Cup fourth round soccer match between Fleetwood Town and Arsenal at Highbury Stadium. (is associated with: «Arsenal stunned by fourth-tier Fleetwood as underdogs win shoot-out») Nick Potts/PA Wire/dpa Fourth-division Fleetwood shocked Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out to advance to the League Cup quarter-finals after a 1-1 draw on Tuesday. Bruno Guimaraes saw his spot-kick saved by Jay Lynch before Fleetwood's teenage defender Conor Haughey lashed home an emphatic penalty. It sparked a pitch invasion at Highbury Stadium as hosts Fleetwood triumphed 5-3 in one of the greatest upsets in the competition's history. Fleetwood, 18th in the fourth tier, dared to dream after Fulham loanee Aaron Loupalo-Bi put them in front after 21 minutes against a much-changed Arsenal side struggling to find any fluidity on the North West coast. The half-time introduction of Martin Odegaard changed the game as the Gunners looked much improved after the break, drawing level in the 50th minute when Viktor Gyokeres just about managed to turn in his first goal of the season. But as Arsenal turned up the heat without reward, their frustration boiled over as their teenage prodigy Max Dowman was sent off with five minutes left to play. There was still time for Lynch to make huge saves from Ben White and Odegaard before it went to a shoot-out in which Fleetwood were perfect from the spot to secure a historic win. Bradford are through to the League Cup quarter-finals for the first time since they reached Wembley in 2013 with a 2-0 win over Peterborough.

item.title: 49ers announce roster moves after monster DeForest Buckner trade
item.description: Credit: Stan Szeto-USA TODAY Sports 49ers announce roster moves after monster DeForest Buckner trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers announced additional roster moves Tuesday after reacquiring three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts ahead of the NFL trade deadline. San Francisco signed defensive lineman Kevin Givens to its practice squad and released wide receiver Malik Turner from the practice squad as the organization continued adjusting its roster following the blockbuster trade. The 49ers confirmed the transactions Tuesday via X, formerly known as Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The #49ers today announced they have signed DL Kevin Givens to the team’s practice squad and released WR Malik Turner from the practice squad.” The moves came hours after San Francisco acquired Buckner from Indianapolis in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick, bringing the veteran defensive tackle back to the organization that selected him seventh overall in the 2016 NFL Draft. Buckner spent his first four NFL seasons with San Francisco before the 49ers traded him to Indianapolis in 2020 for a first-round selection . The 32-year-old now returns to a familiar defensive system as San Francisco looks to strengthen its defensive front heading into the second half of the season. San Francisco’s latest roster adjustments follow Sunday’s disappointing 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 . The defeat ended the 49ers’ undefeated start and dropped them to 6-1, although they remain among the NFC’s top contenders. Adding Buckner provides San Francisco with an experienced interior defensive lineman as the team attempts to regain momentum following its first setback. The 49ers will have a bye in Week 8 before returning home to host the Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) in Week 9 on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1:25 p.m. PT on Fox. Related: Why DeForest Buckner trade is so crucial for 49ers’ success Related: 49ers’ George Kittle excited for boys to be back in town after DeForest Buckner trade

item.title: Why the state of Texas has no sure things for College Football Playoff
item.description: UTSA Roadrunners head coach Jeff Traylor after the game against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) I knew dang near nothing, and proved it. Way back in August, when the email inbox delivered an assignment to make a bunch of college football predictions with fellow Hearst newspaper columnists from around the state, there was little doubt this would end badly. While my esteemed, ever-conscientious colleagues in Austin and Dallas and Houston had been poring over transfer-portal rankings and evaluating preseason practice reports, I'd pretty much had my feet up after following the local cagers through the NBA Finals. As it turned out, a catch-up cram session didn't help much. I picked a national champion that's already lost three times and fallen out of the Top 25, and a national runner-up that lost to BYU , and a Heisman Trophy winner who underperformed before suffering an injury from which he's not likely to return this season. But when it came time to predict how many teams from Texas – a state loaded in the preseason with supposed championship contenders – might make the College Football Playoff? Without a good answer, my instinct was to ask what seemed like a preposterous question: "What if it's zero?" A couple of months later, that question still applies. Texas, which climbed as high as No. 1 in September, still is hanging around the playoff conversation after treating a run of double-digit leads the way the Spurs did in the NBA Finals, but the Longhorns don't inspire much confidence. After two meltdowns against unranked opponents, Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning and Texas' vaunted artificial intelligence apparatus still have trips to Missouri, LSU and Texas A&M on the schedule. Maybe they can get in with a third loss. But it wouldn't be a surprise to see them suffer a fourth one. If the Longhorns need a reason to be optimistic, one might be that the only real resistance the Aggies have put up this season has been against their most dedicated message-board posters . Coach Mike Elko later apologized for referring to the TexAgs online community as a "cesspool." But it's probably wise not to specify what part of a house's plumbing infrastructure that 15 th place in the Southeastern Conference represents. The Aggies are out of the playoff running, and the only race that Baylor and TCU have left over the next month is the one to get mentioned in the most internet articles speculating about trying to hire UTSA's Jeff Traylor. More on the Roadrunners in a bit. In terms of non-SEC schools, Texas Tech was supposed to be the state's safest bet, but that was before it became obvious why the Red Raiders were working so hard to finagle eligibility for the transfer quarterback who ran afoul of NCAA gambling rules. item.title: 3 Wide Receiver Trades That Could Help Rams Survive Davante Adams Injury
item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The Los Angeles Rams have been shopping for a wide receiver with Devante Adams out for multiple weeks , and a handful of trade-market players could be meaningful upgrades. Injuries have hit the Rams hard all year, with key players lost on both sides of the ball, but no position has been more injured than receivers. Puka Nacua missed multiple weeks early in the season after playing Week 1, and once things looked good, Adams went down with a hamstring injury. Additionally, Terrance Ferguson has been on the IR, while the complementary receivers down the depth chart have also missed time. May 28, 2025; Woodland Hills, CA, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Devante Adams (17) walks to the locker room after organized team activities at Rams Practice Facility. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Now, with the trade deadline approaching in a matter of weeks, the Rams’ window to strike is closing. Here are three targets who offer the biggest upgrade at third-down receiver. Brian Thomas Jr. Thomas Jr. had a sensational rookie year, with 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his sophomore and third years have been less than stellar. He has only 812 yards since his rookie campaign, now more than a season and a half. Thomas has plenty of tools and a proven track record of production. With the Jaguars, he has struggled since Liam Chohen took over, which is a red flag since Sean McVay runs a similar system, but Thomas can line up outside and in the slot, giving him versatility, and a possible fresh start may unlock him going forward. McVay has a great track record of developing talent, and Thomas Jr. could be his latest project. Thomas is at the high end of the wide receiver market, costing around a second-round pick. Josh Downs Downs is a receiver who is still more theory than a proven commodity, since he has been pegged as a breakout candidate but has never put together a truly great season. Still, while he hasn’t had a top-flight season, he’s been a machine at creating explosive plays downfield, and he is a true man-beater who can complement Nacua’s skill set against zone coverage. Oct 25, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay during the second half at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Downs might be a step down in terms of price compared to Thomas since he is about to be a free agent. The Rams may only need to cough up a fourth-round pick, maybe a third-rounder at the most, for a half season of Downs. Jaunan Jennnings Finally, Jennings is the lowest-cost option for the Rams. He will require a Day 3 draft pick, has a low salary cap hit, and offers plenty of experience. item.title: College Football TV Ratings: Tracking the most-watched games of the 2026 season
item.description: Last year, college football saw its TV ratings surge and looked to keep the trend going in 2026. item.title: H.S. Roundup | Local athletes shine as postseason play heats up
item.description: The postseason is heating up for area cross country, volleyball and girls and boys soccer teams. Several area teams have their mark already as they continue in tournament play. Several cross country teams have advanced to the regional meet, while volleyball and soccer teams weave their way through district tournament play. CROSS COUNTRY Liberty Union: The Liberty Union Cross Country teams competed at the Central District Cross Country Championships at Hilliard Darby High School on October 24. The girls team placed fourth in D-IV Section 1, qualifying for regionals, and were led by Rachel Sponseller (13th, 20:25). She was followed by Emily Shultz (19th, 21:23), Norah Chaney (21st, 21:35), Ellie Spangler (24th, 21:59), Taylor Jones (35th, 23:16), Rylan Myers (36th, 23:23) and Alaina Brate (52nd, 25:24). More: Lancaster volleyball rallies past Kilbourne to punch ticket to district final The boys team placed third in D-IV Section 1, qualifying for regionals, and were led by William McCreery (12th, 17:05). He was followed by Levi Hendershot (26th, 19:42), Silas Kohler (29th, 19:57), William Gonzalez (30th, 20:05), Chad Valentine (31st, 20:07), Micah Fisher (32nd, 20:20) and Christopher Bisel (37th, 20:54). Fairfield Union: The Fairfield Union boys and girls won the Southeast District Championships. For the girls, it was their 11 th district title in the last 12 years. Leading the way, Sadie Schultz was named Southeast District Runner of the Year, while Coach Rob Myers earned Southeast District Coach of the Year honors. The Falcons had four girls earn first-team all-district honors. item.title: Pisacane concedes: “Roma are unstoppable.”
item.description: Pisacane concedes: “Roma are unstoppable.” Cagliari coach Fabio Pisacane, after the 4-2 loss to Roma, analyzed his team’s defeat to DAZN. On Cagliari’s performance and the defeat “Certainly, tonight, seeing the demands we want to make, seeing the attitude the team showed in the match, which must never be lacking, are two elements we must pack and take to Cagliari. I think coming here to put in a performance like that, as I told the boys, I want to lose matches, but I don’t want to lose them like this, without leaving Caprile in my arms. Sometimes, it was also the opponents who forced us to play a more submissive game.” “I think the team achieved much more than they deserved in the first six games, but in the end, football balances out. They’re a young team, with few experienced players. The goal is to get everyone back and play the football we want to continue.” “It’s normal in football, as you know better than I, that the winner is always the winner. We had a battleship up front that made things difficult for everyone, but I enjoyed the performance the team played, with great dignity, with the right attitude, and I’m convinced that as we grow like this, everything will turn around again.”

item.title: Xabi Alonso’s return to Liverpool felt inevitable – behind the scenes, the reality was always different
item.description: A wonderful long passer and a midfielder with the capacity to score from the halfway line, Xabi Alonso always seemed to have the ability to plot the way to a far-off target with expert precision. For years, the theory was that it would transport the former Liverpool midfielder to the dugouts at Anfield. When it has, though, it has been the opposition technical area: first with Bayer Leverkusen , then Real Madrid , the other club with whom he won the Champions League, now with Chelsea , the club beaten on Merseyside in two Champions League semi-finals two decades ago. A man who created many a Liverpool goal has promised he will celebrate “for sure” if Chelsea score at Anfield on Wednesday; he had nothing to celebrate in 2024, however, when his Leverkusen were walloped 4-0 , or last year, when his Real lost 1-0 . Alonso has returned to Anfield with Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid but coming back with Chelsea for the Carabao Cup fourth round will bring a different atmosphere (Getty) The chant in Alonso’s playing days, when Liverpool represented the ancien regime and Chelsea the nouveau riche , was that the Londoners “ain’t got no history”. Liverpool and Alonso have plenty; he scored their first goal against AC Milan in “the miracle of Istanbul”, and they spiralled into decline after his 2009 sale to Real. When he took Leverkusen to an unbeaten double, he looked a Liverpool manager in waiting. Now the wait may be never-ending. When Jurgen Klopp announced in January 2024 that he would stand down, Alonso seemed the best candidate. Including, it soon transpired, to Klopp himself, who appeared to give the Basque his blessing as his successor. Describing managers of his vintage as dinosaurs, the German said: “The next generation is already there and I would say Xabi is standout.” Whether or not the Liverpool hierarchy at the time concurred, they were soon deterred. While Bayern Munich mounted a public chase of Alonso, Liverpool did not. “At that time, I was at Leverkusen and I was aware of the situation but I decided to stay,” he said. He never spoke to Liverpool. The greater surprise, perhaps, was that he did not in 2026, either. Two years ago, after Ruben Amorim was wrongly described as the frontrunner, Arne Slot was instead appointed. Slot won a Premier League title while Madrid, the third superclub Alonso represented, hired him a year later. Yet his sacking by Real in January felt like a case of bad timing for an increasingly beleaguered Slot . Alonso’s sudden availability made him the obvious alternative, the king over the water. The idea of Alonso was seductive to many a Liverpool fan, if not to their hierarchy. They did not intervene when Chelsea made their move for a man who once had his ankle broken by Frank Lampard in one of the many flashpoints of a rivalry that had a bitterness when Rafa Benitez and Jose Mourinho patrolled the technical areas. Alonso became a great at Anfield while Liverpool’s rivalry with Chelsea peaked on the pitch (Getty)

item.title: Lubbock High's Anderson, Frenship boys lead Region I-5A cross country results
item.description: Amelia Anderson is heading back to the UIL state meet. The Lubbock High sophomore won the Region I-5A cross country title with a 5K time of 18 minutes, 0.6 seconds Tuesday, Oct. 27 at Mae Simmons Park. Anderson finished 38.5 seconds ahead of runner-up Sayuri Ulloa of El Paso Burges. As a freshman, Anderson placed ninth in the Class 5A state meet. She will again be joined by a Lubbock ISD classmate. Monterey's Hannah Hughes finished sixth Tuesday in 19:11.1. The pair are the lone local state qualifiers on the girls side, although Frenship's Jentri Duffield (19:43.3) and Frenship Memorial's Morgan Roller (19:47.5) finished 13th and 17th, respectively. On the boys side, Lubbock High's Arturo Rodriguez was regional runner-up in 15:54.2. LISD had two other individuals advance to state in Coronado's Ellis Jackson (5th, 16:05.7) and Monterey's Julius Garcia (8th, 16:12.3). Frenship's Braxton Johnson placed ninth in 16:15.0 to lead the Tigers to a third-place finish and state berth as a team. Frenship totaled 158 points behind Jacob Dominguez (27th), Jonathan Murray (28th), Jacob Murray (40th) and Kason Autrey (57th). The 5A state meet is scheduled for Nov. 7 at Old Settlers Park in Round Rock. item.title: Chicago sports radio personalities not sad to see John Schriffen go: ‘The White Sox can do better’
item.description: Credit: 670 The Score, CSN On Monday, the Chicago White Sox announced that they would not extend the contract of John Schriffen , the team’s lead TV play-by-play voice since 2024. It does sound as though there are too many people around Chicago sports radio all that broken up about it. The 42-year-old Schriffen became the team’s lead television play-by-play broadcaster before the 2024 season , replacing Jason Benetti, who left to become the voice of the Detroit Tigers amid issues related to the organization . Replacing Benetti, a celebrated national voice, was an uphill climb, and Schriffen faced heavy criticism including an intense feud with Chicago radio host Matt Spiegel. The 670 The Score host took the announcer to task over his perceived lack of baseball knowledge . Schriffen responded to that criticism, referring to ‘ radio losers ‘ in response. There was also some handshake-related drama when they met in person that cemented the disdain. After the news broke on Monday, Spiegel shared his thoughts on Spiegel & Holmes, saying that while he thought the White Sox announcer had improved, it was nowhere near what the franchise needed. Matt Spiegel on the White Sox letting John Schriffen go: “I’ve held back my feelings for the better part of two years since being very vocal on them in year one because I didn’t want to punch at a guy who was out here just trying to do his job. But this is a moment for me to be honest. I think he was terrible. I think the White Sox can do better, and they will do better.” — 104.3 The Score (@thescorechicago) October 26, 2026 “I do believe that he got better to an extent,” said Spiegel. “but I think there were plenty of moments this year where I was still like, man, watch the game. Just think the game. Just feel the freaking game. And it wasn’t happening. “I also personally had trouble with what seemed like a lack of authenticity as I felt it. Like, it needs to be a really comfortable feel for me to hang out with a play-by-play person for a long time, and I didn’t really get that from John. But that’s me personally. “I’ve held back my feelings for the better part of two years since being very vocal on them in year one, because I didn’t want to punch at a guy who was out here just trying to do his job. But this is a moment for me to be honest. I think he was terrible, and I think the White Sox can do better, and they will do better.” Dan Bernstein took it a step further. The former 670 The Score host , who now hosts Dan Bernstein Unfiltered on the 312 Sports Network, said that the news only makes him angrier than Benetti is no longer the TV voice of the Sox. “I’m not celebrating [John Schriffen departing the White Sox broadcasts], and here’s why. It reaffirms and rekindles my distaste over the fact that Jason Benetti isn’t the White Sox guy for the rest of his life,” said Bernstein on Monday’s episode . “Or at least hasn’t been in a position here where he’s got the chance if he wants, as he goes about everything else

item.title: Fantasy Football Impact: 4 Potential Josh Downs Landing Spots
item.description: Dec 14, 2025; Seattle, Washington, USA; Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs (2) runs into the end zone for a touchdown after catching a pass against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With how the Indianapolis Colts' 2026 season has gone, they seem to have transitioned to a full-on fire sale of their roster. On Tuesday, Oct. 27, they dealt G Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and DE DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. Another Colts player who has a real chance to be on the move as well is WR Josh Downs. According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz, teams that are in need of a WR have been calling the Colts about Downs ' availability. With that, here are four teams that make sense as suitors for Downs, and a breakdown of what his fantasy football value would look like on their team. Pittsburgh Steelers It would not be surprising if the Pittsburgh Steelers were in the market for WR depth. Both Steelers WRs Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. are on the injured reserve. And with Aaron Rodgers as their QB, they are clearly looking to compete right now. If Downs were to get traded to Pittsburgh, as the Steelers roster currently is with Wilson and Pittman Jr. out, he would likely play the role of WR3. His fantasy value would take a slight hit from where it currently stands with the Colts, and rookie WR Germie Bernard's value would also take a fairly significant hit. Downs is a good short-yardage WR, which is an area that Bernard has consistently made an impact for the Steelers in their last three games. Arizona Cardinals After trading away their WR2, Marvin Harrison Jr., the Arizona Cardinals are in need of a WR. In the absence of Harrison Jr., no WR has really stepped up and put forth notable production to firmly grab that WR2 spot, so Downs, if he were traded to Arizona, could take on that WR2 role right away. Downs' fantasy value would go up from where it currently is in Indianapolis. The Cardinals this season have been an extremely pass-heavy offense. They are averaging the most pass attempts per game in the NFL, 40.4. San Francisco 49ers The 49ers make a ton of sense as a potential team that Down could get traded to. They are definite Super Bowl contenders, and one of the main positions where they have had major injury problems this season is at WR. Both 49ers WRs Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel did not play in Week 7 due to injuries. They are also without WR Ricky Pearsall, who had season-ending surgery on his right knee. They did just get WR Christian Kirk back from the IR, but with the inconsistencies in health they have had at WR, San Francisco needs to add depth. Downs' fantasy value would decrease if Evans and Samuel were available; with them out, it would rise, and he would be a must-start. item.title: Barcelona star Lamine Yamal issues official response to missing out on Ballon d’Or
item.description: Barcelona star Lamine Yamal issues official response to missing out on Ballon d’Or Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has on Tuesday taken to social media, to issue an official response to missing out on the Ballon d’Or award. Attacker Lamine was of course in attendance yesterday evening, as the Ballon d’Or gala was held in front of a packed crowd at the London Palladium. The 19-year-old was considered to be amongst the very frontrunners for the accolade, after a spectacular year culminating in glory in both La Liga and at the World Cup. When all was said and done, though, Lamine was forced to make do with a place in 3rd, behind Kylian Mbappé, and ‘Golden Ball’ winner Harry Kane. Upon cameras panning to the Barcelona prodigy at the gala, Lamine looked nothing short of devastated with the outcome. With the dust having since settled on the ceremony, and the young winger having had time to mull things over, though, Lamine has taken to his official social media platforms, to unveil the following statement: “It’ll come. Good things take time, and I trust the path I’m building. There’s no rush. I’m full of hope and confidence that one day my moment will come. “Congratulations to the winners. My focus now returns to what really matters: helping Barcelona win again.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Arsenal stunned by fourth-tier Fleetwood in League Cup
item.description: Fleetwood striker Aaron Loupalo-Bi celebrates scoring against Arsenal (Darren Staples) Arsenal suffered one of the most humiliating defeats in their history as the Premier League champions were stunned by fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in a League Cup penalty shoot-out on Tuesday. Mikel Arteta's side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time. Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out and Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood's winner. Aaron Loupalo-Bi's first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval. Arsenal's 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages. Arteta paid the price for prioritising Sunday's Premier League trip to Liverpool as his decision to make nine changes backfired spectacularly. No one would have predicted Arsenal's embarrassment regardless of Arteta's selection gamble. They had moved level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City after a 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday. But instead of extending their run of 11 wins from their 13 previous games, Arsenal returned to north London red-faced after a loss that ranks among the darkest days in the club's glittering history. Arsene Wenger's Arsenal suffered a shock League Cup loss against fourth tier Bradford on penalties in 2012. Arteta's team were beaten by second tier Southampton in the FA Cup last season and also lost to Nottingham Forest, then in the Championship, in the same competition in 2022. Supporters of an older vintage will recall Arsenal's 1969 League Cup final loss against third tier Swindon and their 1992 FA Cup exit at fourth tier Wrexham. But even those painful defeats cannot compare to this remarkable result. For once, Arsenal fans will not have fond memories of Highbury -- Fleetwood's ground shares the same name as the Gunners' ancestral home before their move to the Emirates Stadium in 2006. Fleetwood's tiny 5,327-capacity ground -- where goals are celebrated with a burst of children' cartoon song Captain Pugwash over the tannoy -- is a far cry from the famous marble halls and dignified grandeur of Arsenal's former stadium. Now it will be remembered forever as the site of Arsenal's most chastening loss in the Arteta era. Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor wept tears of joy as disbelieving fans flooded the pitch to celebrate their club's astonishing victory. - 'Cod Army' uprising - Only Myles Lewis-Skelly and Viktor Gyokeres kept their places from the Everton game, with teenagers Dowman and Marli Salmon starting, while 18-year-old winger Ceadach O'Neill made his debut. Languishing in 18th place in League Two, Fleetwood had lost their previous two league games against Exeter and Cheltenham, yet they showed no signs of being intimidated by their illustrious visitors. item.title: Former Grand Slam winner Wawrinka ends tennis career
item.description: Stan Wawrinka bid farewell to tennis as he brought the curtain down on a decorated 24-year career following a first-round exit at the Basel Open on Tuesday. The 41-year-old Swiss announced earlier in the season that his last tournament as a professional would be the ATP 500-level event in his home country and a 7-5, 7-6 (7/2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka brought an end to the career of the three-time major champion. Former world number three Wawrinka, along with Andy Murray, was the only player to win multiple Grand Slams in a period dominated by Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic. He bested Nadal to win his first Grand Slam at the Australian Open in 2014, before beating Djokovic in the French Open final the following season and then again in the US Open title-match in 2016. Alongside his compatriot Federer, the Lausanne native won the Davis Cup for Switzerland and claimed gold in the doubles at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. On court in Basel, Wawrinka’s every point won, as well as several trademark booming one-handed backhands, was greeted by wild cheers from the partisan home crowd. But Lehecka got his nose in front with a break of serve in the 11th game and sealed the opening set with an ace as he held to love. A tight second set rumbled towards a tie-break, but it was just a step too far for Wawrinka as his 21st-ranked opponent took firm control to seal the breaker and the match. The post Former Grand Slam winner Wawrinka ends tennis career appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Cleveland Browns WR up for a league honor after big game in Week 7
item.description: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) Cleveland Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion had the type of day on Sunday that he and the Browns have been waiting for since he was selected in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft. Concepcion finished the game against the Tennessee Titans with eight receptions for 129 yards and 23 rushing yards, including an 18-yard scamper in the fourth quarter that helped set up a touchdown. The 129 receiving yards are the eighth-most by a rookie in a single game in franchise history , placing Concepcion in the company of notable players like Paul Warfield, Kevin Johnson, and Webster Slaughter. While pleased with his stats in Cleveland’s latest comeback victory, after the game Concepcion said he believes this should be the norm rather than the exception : “I enter every week expecting to have a game like this. This week was my breakout game. I just can’t wait to keep stacking weeks. I’ve been this way all my life. I play this game with so much heart, so much effort. I’m finally glad that Browns fans and the Browns community were finally able to see what I can bring to this team.” The Titans were not the only ones who took notice of Concepcion’s big day, but the NFL did as well as Concepcion has been nominated for Rookie of the Week honors for Week 7. Who should be the @pepsi Rookie of the Week for Week 7? Vote in the poll below! ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/RiClxCg3W2 — NFL (@NFL) October 27, 2026 Concepcion leads the Browns in receptions (30), is second in receiving yards (315) to fellow rookie Denzel Boston, and is one of eight Cleveland players averaging more than 10 yards per reception. The other players nominated for the award are: New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., who had five receptions for 115 yards and one touchdown Miami Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas, who had two receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns Atlanta Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels, who has 11 tackles, one interception, and one fumble recovery Fan voting takes place on Instagram or X (@NFL) through Thursday at 11 a.m. EST. item.title: Super Bowl-Winning QB Urges Minnesota Vikings to Make Blockbuster Trade for $44M Pro Bowler
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Vikings are the last undefeated team left, and general manager Nolan Teasley has surely been busy working the trade lines as he navigates his first trade deadline in an enviable position. Will the Vikings capitalize on their hot start? The belief is the Vikings will be making a move of some kind before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, and a former Super Bowl-winning quarterback knows exactly who Kevin O’Connell’s team should be targeting. Related: 6-Step Plan to Build 6-0 Minnesota Vikings Into Super Bowl Champions Russell Wilson Wants Minnesota Vikings to Add Jonathan Taylor to Unleash Kyler Murray and Justin Jefferson Oct 25, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) rushes the ball against the Minnesota Vikings in the first half at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Rempel-Imagn Images The Vikings could address a number of needs, from the interior offensive line, a blocking tight end, another pass-rushing DT, a rotational edge rusher, or a safety to further strengthen the NFL’s best defense. Yet, the better approach may be to add a difference-maker who can unlock the potential within coach O’Connell’s offense, and the perfect target may or may not be available. Appearing on CBS’ “ Set Hut ” alongside Chris Long, former Super Bowl-winning quarterback Russell Wilson urged the Vikings to get aggressive and trade for Jonathan Taylor . “Maybe we knock on the door of Jonathan Taylor and see if we can get that running game going with Aaron Jones and have a two-tandem running back system. He’s got 140 rushes already, 587 yards, this is just this season. You know who knows how to score touchdowns? This guy knows how to score touchdowns, he’s got eight of ’em already and Daniel Jones isn’t playing good in Indy.” Russell Wilson on Jonathan Taylor Trade to Vikings The First-Team All-Pro would give the Vikings one of the best running backs in the NFL, whose combined speed, power, and excellent vision to record at least 1,000 yards from scrimmage in five of the past six seasons. It’s also Wilson’s belief that the three-time Pro Bowl running back would make life easier for Murray and even Justin Jefferson, opening up more opportunities downfield, with the front seven keying in on trying to slow down Taylor too. “What could he do if you gave Kyler Murray a running back? Let him put under center, downhill runs, play-action. Get the ball deep down the field. Justin Jefferson needs to have at least a go ball a quarter. We gotta be throwing the ball to him no matter what. If there’s two guys on him, still, throw it to him, it’s a him route, it doesn’t matter, but when you got a guy like this, it makes it a one-high defense, 1-on-1 matchups for Justin Jefferson.” Wilson on How Taylor Trade Would Impact Vikings Trade matchmaker @DangeRussWilson believes Jonathan Taylor could be the missing ingredient for the Vikings offense 👀 #SetHut https://t.co/c6ObMTb4qo — NFL on CBS 🏈

item.title: Michael Penix Jr., Pat Mahomes, and 2 More Must-Sit Quarterbacks in Week 8 Fantasy Football
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) makes a throw against the San Francisco 49ers during the fourth quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Unless your quarterback is named Josh Allen or Brock Purdy, I cannot say that they are weekly plug-and-plays in fantasy football. It is a tough, unpredictable game, for that matter. That brings me to an extensive statistical analysis that labels the following four quarterbacks as benchable in Week 8. Baker Mayfield The intrigue is well-placed following a 43-point win after Week 7. But Mayfield is not startable. He played in Week 7 with gloves on, which he said would affect his grip and his throwing mechanics, and it contributed to him throwing the ball only 11 times. The thumb injury will linger all year. Until we see Mayfield pass more and do it effectively, he can't start, despite the Buccaneers' offensive breakout. Sam Darnold Darnold has 8 interceptions through six games. He ties Drake Maye and Justin Herbert for the most interceptions in the NFL. He is also being sacked 2.3 times per game, the 10th-worst among all 32 current starting quarterbacks. The Bears face Seattle this week. They rank 10th in EPA per Pass Allowed, 7th-best in Success Rate, and 7th in Total Sacks. After seeing how well Kirk Cousins is doing in Las Vegas, I firmly believe that Darnold misses Klint Kubiak as his play-caller. Michael Penix Jr. Penix Jr. has 7 touchdowns and 0 interceptions over his last three games. Nonetheless, I would avoid starting him in fantasy football. Penix Jr. does not run the football. He has 12 attempts for 4 yards and 3 fumbles. Only two quarterbacks in the fantasy football top 10 have fewer than 60 rushing yards this season. Those two top-10 quarterbacks average at least 2.0 passing touchdowns per game (Jared Goff, Bryce Young). The Buccaneers topple onto this "sit" case, ranked 3rd in EPA per Pass Allowed, 8th in Success Rate, and 5th in Interception Rate. Pat Mahomes The Chiefs have been in a romance with their running game. They are running the ball 27 times per game for 5.3 Yards per Attempt. In the red zone, they have run the ball 34 times, compared to 30 passing attempts. Mahomes is averaging only 1.5 passing touchdowns per game and ranks QB19 in fantasy football in average points per game. The Broncos face the Chiefs this weekend. They rank 4th in EPA per Pass Allowed and 4th in Success Rate. The Chiefs also don't know whether Rashee Rice will return to the field. No Chiefs wide receiver is ranked in the top 40 in Receiving EPA per Target. item.title: Gasperini: ‘A precious Roma win, youth players have talent’
item.description: Gasperini: ‘A precious Roma win, youth players have talent’ Gian Piero Gasperini feels the difficulties caused by Cagliari made the 4-2 Roma win ‘more precious’ and is glad to see two goals from youth academy products. The Giallorossi were made to work very hard for the three points this evening, against a Cagliari side that had lost its last two Serie A matches. Niccolò Pisilli’s handling offence prompted an early M’Bala Nzola penalty, only for Emanuele Lulli and Pisilli to turn it around within 12 minutes. Pierluigi Gollini kept his men in front until the Daniel Maldini equaliser, but substitutes Rodrigo Mora and Donyell Malen secured the 4-2 victory late on. Gasperini relishing Roma victory ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: Donyell Malen of AS Roma scores his team’s fourth goal during the Serie A match between AS Roma and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on October 27, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) “Undoubtedly, we had a few difficulties today,” Gasperini confessed to DAZN Italia. “They were fresher in attack and created problems for us. We are also using the same elements in midfield for every game and the fatigue is starting to show. That makes our victory even more precious, because everyone was involved.” Check the Football Italia Player Ratings for Roma 4-2 Cagliari Daniele Ghilardi came off the bench and provided the cross for the Rodrigo Mora header. “Ghilardi had some very good performances recently, he probably should’ve come on earlier today, but it was a tough change to make. He has improved so much compared to last season and will get more space.” ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: Emanuele Lulli of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s first goal with teammate Gianluca Mancini during the Serie A match between AS Roma and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on October 27, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Roma have to rotate the squad in order to deal with their packed fixture list, especially now that they are in the Champions League after a seven-year absence. There are also injuries to Paulo Dybala, Mile Svilar, Manu Koné and Lorenzo Pellegrini to limit the alternatives, but despite that, Rodrigo Mora still can’t seem to get into the starting XI. “It’s not easy to play so many games without Dybala and Kone, so we can make mistakes, but winning against a difficult side like Cagliari is something to be proud of.” The injury to Mile Svilar was the most unexpected and serious, but Gollini really has stepped up to the plate. “He didn’t play 112 games at the top level by accident. I worked with him at Atalanta when he was still a kid, more exuberant and less eager to work hard. We met again here at Roma, but I never had doubts over his qualities.” ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 27: Niccolo Pisilli of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the Serie A match between AS Roma and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on October 27, 2026 in Rome, Italy. item.title: Dave Doeren rues transfer portal for stealing NFL talent from NC State after being fired
item.description: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images Dave Doeren rues transfer portal for stealing NFL talent from NC State after being fired appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The North Carolina State football program is looking for a new head coach. Dave Doeren was fired following a rough start to the 2026 season. Doeren is opening up about what happened at his NC State program, before he was given the boot. The coach knows his program lost talent to the transfer portal in recent years, and it hurt the Wolfpack. “We’ve lost on average four potential NFL players — or NFL players — in each of the last three years. It’s sad to say, but that’s where football is now. It’s in a state of do you have enough NIL to retain and acquire what you need to have a competitive depth chart?” Doeren said, per On3. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Doeren had coached at NC State for more than a decade. After he took over the program in 2013, he posted 10 total winning seasons. “I love this university, and I leave here knowing that I made it better than I found it — on and off the field. I wanted so badly to win a championship here at NC State, but I will be cheering for this program to get there under its future leadership,” Doeren said, per On3. North Carolina State is now looking for its next head coach . Some candidates for the job include former Wolfpack star Philip Rivers, who played quarterback at the school. He then went on to a long career in the NFL. “Since 2021, Rivers has been coaching high school football in Alabama, including his son Gunner, an SC Next 300 prospect who is committed to NC State for 2027. The father-son combination could appeal to NC State, especially if Rivers, 44, can build a strong staff,” ESPN reported. This season, North Carolina State is 3-4 overall. The team is also 1-3 in the ACC. NC State next plays California on Saturday. item.title: Kordell Stewart Slash & Burn: What to Know About Documentary on Former Steelers QB
item.description: Kordell Stewart Slash & Burn: What to Know About Documentary on Former Steelers QB originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . If you grew up rooting for the Steelers in the 1990s, you likely had a Kordell Stewart jersey in your closet. The former Pittsburgh star earned the nickname "Slash" after jumping from Colorado to the NFL and making an impact at multiple positions. Long before mobile quarterbacks like Lamar Jackson and Josh Allen were dodging defenders, Stewart was lining up at wide receiver. "I did everything under the sun, from punting, catching, throwing, running," Stewart said during an interview with CBS analysts Kyle Long and Russell Wilson. "Then, all of a sudden, I got my opportunity to start in 1997. And then I showed I was capable of being a full-time quarterback in the National Football League." Stewart went 11-5 in his first year as Pittsburgh's starter with 32 total touchdowns. He set career highs with 3,109 passing yards and 537 rushing yards in 2001, finishing fourth in MVP voting. But he also faced significant challenges on and off the field. Stewart had to deal with unsubstantiated rumors alleging that he was arrested for engaging in lewd acts with a man at a local park. Despite the lack of evidence surrounding the allegations and Stewart's firm denial , the rumors lingered. He only lasted one more season in Pittsburgh after his stellar 2001 campaign, ending his career with short stints in Chicago (2003) and Baltimore (2004-05). "Kordell Stewart: Slash & Burn," a new HBO documentary, will cover the rise and fall of one of the most thrilling players in Steelers history. The documentary will also be available to stream on HBO Max. item.title: NFL Insider teases more Colts trades coming after Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner trades
item.description: © Grace Smith-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images NFL Insider teases more Colts trades coming after Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner trades appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts may not be finished making moves ahead of the NFL trade deadline after dealing All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner on Tuesday. NFL insider Jordan Schultz suggested that Indianapolis could continue its roster overhaul following the team’s 16-10 Week 7 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. “The #Colts may not be done yet either…” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Schultz shared the message Tuesday via X, formerly known as Twitter, shortly after Indianapolis completed two significant trades involving longtime franchise cornerstones. The Colts began Tuesday by sending Nelson to the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection. Nelson, a seven-time Pro Bowl selection and three-time first-team All-Pro, had been a cornerstone of Indianapolis’ offensive line since the organization selected him sixth overall in the 2018 NFL Draft. Hours later, Indianapolis traded Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick , sending the veteran defensive tackle back to the organization where he began his NFL career. Colts could continue roster overhaul ahead of trade deadline Buckner originally joined the Colts in 2020 after Indianapolis acquired him from San Francisco in exchange for a first-round selection. The departures of Nelson and Buckner represent a significant shift for an Indianapolis organization that entered the season hoping to compete in the AFC South. With the Colts sitting at 2-5 following consecutive losses, the organization appears willing to move established veterans in exchange for future draft capital. Schultz did not identify any additional players Indianapolis could move, leaving uncertainty surrounding the team’s next potential transaction. The Colts will look to snap their losing streak when they visit the Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) in Week 8 on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. item.title: French Footballer Kylian Mbappé Faces Backlash In China After Viral Clip Shows Him Discussing 'Dictator Mbappe' Meme
item.description: French pro footballer Kylian Mbappé has become controversial in China after a clip of him referring to a "Chinese dictator" went viral over the last day. The dictator in question is Mao Zedong, leading multiple Chinese brands to drop Mbappé’s deals with them. Mbappé has since issued an apology to China and the Chinese people as the controversy surrounding the incident continues generating discourse online. Soccer star Kylian Mbappé is famous for representing France internationally, including winning the 2018 FIFA World Cup for his country. He has consistently scored for France in the two World Cup editions that followed, as well as in other international tournaments, and captains France’s National Soccer Team since 2023. He has also become a notable player for France’s Paris Saint-Germain and Spain’s Real Madrid, the latter of which is his current club. However, the renowned athlete found himself at the center of a controversy in China for an answer he gave during an interview with The Bridge, a French talk show, in a short clip that was posted to its social media, and which they have since deleted. In the clip, Mbappé talks about a version of the popular "Dictator Mbappé" meme, which depicts him as a Chinese dictator, among other dictator-like personas. 😂🇫🇷 Kylian Mbappé avoue qu’il rigole en voyant les memes qui le représentent en… dictateur. 😭 @Thebridge_show #Mbappé #Football #Memes #France https://t.co/MXgKh8Hjjq — Que Du Foot (@Que_Du_Football) October 26, 2026 In the video, Mbappé is seen holding a microphone as someone applies make-up on his face as questions appear on text on top of the video in French. The first question is about his favorite artist at the moment, and he answers, also in French. Then, he gets asked to choose his favorite meme. "Um, I think the one with Thierry Henry, you know, when he’s smiling," he answers, "that one’s pretty good, because you can use it in so many different ways." Mbappé then tries to replicate Henry's smile in said meme. Then, the clip gets to the new controversial answer, where Mbappé gets asked what meme with his face made him laugh the most. "Well, there are tons of them," he says. "The one that made me laugh the most was when someone took a video of a guy. I think it was a Chinese dictator. And they added my face to it." As he speaks, the video shows a GIF where Mbappé's face was edited onto the head and body of Mao Zedong, who founded the People’s Republic of China and ruled it for over three decades. A portion of the Soviet communist flag can be seen in the background. "I use it a lot with my friends online, you know, while playing on the PlayStation," Mbappé says. Though Mbappé himself doesn’t mention Mao Zedong by name, it was largely assumed that he was the "Chinese dictator" that he was referring to, as many of the dictator memes superimpose him on imagery of the controversial Chinese leader. item.title: Gasperini analyzes win over Cagliari: “It wasn’t easy, we had several banged-up players.”
item.description: Gasperini analyzes win over Cagliari: “It wasn’t easy, we had several banged-up players.” Gian Piero Gasperini spoke to DAZN after Roma-Cagliari (4-2). The Giallorossi coach commented on his team’s victory: “It’s going very well. We undoubtedly had some players struggling who hadn’t fully recovered. It’s also clear that some of their new players created problems for us. That was the only reason. We always played with the same players in midfield and we saw some signs of fatigue, so it’s even more creditable that we won. Especially at 1-0, we had excellent control, and then also at the end.” The Roma coach on Ghilardi: “He’s had excellent games. He probably should have come on earlier, but then there were situations where it was difficult to make that substitution, otherwise he would have been the first one after half-time. He’s improved a lot compared to last year and will continue to find more space.” Gasperini on the conditions of Balerdi and Hermoso and the absentees: “Balerdi and Hermoso weren’t fit to play. It’s not easy to play so many games without Dybala, Koné, and others. Cristante returned after a month and played two 90-minute games in three days. The win against Cagliari is a great achievement, as they are a tough team to face.” Gian Piero Gasperini spoke about Gollini: “He was a goalkeeper who even played in the Champions League and achieved important goals. At the time, he was younger and more exuberant, less motivated to work and improve. We met again in Rome, and I never had any doubts about his qualities. He trains very well, and I’m happy with what he’s done in recent matches. He’s extraordinary up close, but he concedes goals from distance, but he’s an excellent goalkeeper.” The Giallorossi coach on Lulli and Pisilli: “They’re extraordinary guys. I have to say that there’s always something great going on in the youth academy. There are some guys who are very attached to Roma, and this leads them to dream of making their first-team debuts, and that’s a very positive thing. They’re absolutely talented guys. Lulli scored with a header, and we were training yesterday.” The Grugliasco general on Mora’s goal: “I saw him score a header against Porto: he’s small but he jumps really well. Look at the way he hit the ball: he’s almost standing still and he whips it in and scores a great goal.”

item.title: Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro flees to US after election loss
item.description: Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil and is traveling to the United States despite a court order banning him from exiting the country, US media reported Tuesday. The son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro lost elections to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday and refused to concede defeat. The right-wing senator on Monday said a Supreme Court justice had ordered him to hand over his passports. Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and with his election loss is also set to lose his parliamentary immunity. The 45-year-old was heading to Florida, CNN reported Tuesday, citing an anonymous official source. Other US media confirmed he was heading to the country. The US State Department said Tuesday that it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family, without confirming his travel plans. A police source told AFP that the senator’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, adding that “there is no formal record of Flavio Bolsonaro leaving the country.” But he has held Italian nationality since 2023, according to an Italian parliamentary document seen by AFP. Bolsonaro’s campaign manager Rogerio Marinho expressed shock over reports that the defeated candidate had fled Brazil. “We still don’t have any news about his whereabouts,” he told reporters in Brasilia on Tuesday. “I received a text message from him this morning, where he said he would let some time pass today and then would talk with us, and that was it,” Marinho said. “That was the only communication we had.” – Scare tactic – Flavio Bolsonaro said Monday that the ban on his exit from Brazil amounted to a scare tactic. “I never had any intention of leaving the country. I will surrender my passports and defend myself against this travesty,” he said in the video posted on Instagram. US President Donald Trump, a close ally of Jair Bolsonaro, on Monday said Brazil’s elections were “rigged” following the defeat of Bolsonaro junior. Flavio’s brother Eduardo, a US-based former lawmaker, maintains close ties with the White House. Last week, he told a US podcast that Flavio Bolsonaro should leave Brazil in the event of electoral defeat, given the active probes into his activities. In his Monday statement, Lula’s challenger also said he would lead the opposition to the leftist government. Following Lula’s victory with 51.8 percent of the vote, Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the result, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transportation difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting. Lula had requested the extension, as had Bolsonaro over bad weather in parts of the country. – In his father’s footsteps – All bets were on a Bolsonaro win after he came out on top in the first round of elections earlier this month. He campaigned on a pledge to liberate his father, who is under house arrest for coup-plotting after his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022. Jair Bolsonaro never conceded defeat
